title: Amul and Mother Dairy raise milk prices by Rs 2-4 a litre
body: Amul and Mother Dairy raised liquid milk prices from Thursday, citing higher costs for fodder, cattle feed, packaging and transport. The page puts the increase at Rs 2 to 4 per litre, and Mother Dairy's hike was Rs 4 in a single step. Delhi consumers said earlier revisions were about Re 1 at a time. They complained that prices are revised every few months, which makes monthly budgeting difficult. Some linked the hike to rising inflation and stagnant incomes, and one person asked the government to regulate milk prices.

title: CCPA fines Ola Rs 10 lakh over 'pay extra for a faster ride' tip prompts
body: The Central Consumer Protection Authority fined ANI Technologies, which runs Ola, Rs 10 lakh and ordered it to stop its pre-ride 'tip' or 'add-on' feature. The regulator found the prompts misled riders into thinking that paying more would get them a ride faster. Ola's own data showed that requests with extra payments had lower acceptance rates. Ola kept showing the prompts after a Road Transport Ministry clarification dated August 11. The regulator classed the prompts as a dark pattern and an unfair trade practice. Many riders have complained about these nudges.

title: Spotify launches audiobooks in India as a paid Rs 199 add-on
body: Spotify launched audiobooks in India with an Audiobooks+ plan at Rs 199 a month. The plan gives 15 listening hours a month. Users can top up hours or buy individual titles. The launch catalogue has more than 350,000 English titles and almost 7,000 Indian-language audiobooks. Spotify for Authors also opened to Indian writers. Some outlets pointed out that listeners must pay extra, because a music Premium plan does not include audiobook hours.

title: Jio, Airtel and Vi prepaid plans may cost up to 15% more soon
body: Cashify reports that Jio, Airtel and Vi may raise prepaid prices by up to 15% (12-15% in the highlights) within the next 3 to 4 months. This is an expectation, not a confirmed hike. The page says the last major tariff change was about two years ago, in 2024, and that pricing may move towards usage-based charging that makes heavy data users pay more. Current 84-day plans cost Rs 519 for Jio and Vi and Rs 539 for Airtel. Mobile users already feel squeezed on recharge costs.

title: Madras High Court bars Blinkit from using a CSK superfan's likeness
body: The Madras High Court barred Blinkit from using the likeness of a CSK superfan without his consent. The fan, Saravanan Hari, is seeking Rs 1.1 crore in damages. The next hearing is on 14 December. The case is about a brand using an ordinary person's face in its advertising, and it reached the court after the fan took legal action.

title: SEBI clears MakeMyTrip India IPO
body: SEBI has cleared the IPO of MakeMyTrip's India unit, which filed confidentially in July 2026. Issue size and price band have not been disclosed. MakeMyTrip and ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) will sell shares. The page also says 54 of 69 new-age tech stocks tracked by Inc42 gained in the week ended 7 November. Their combined market value rose 5.2% to $169.3 billion, and CarTrade rose 23.3%.

title: Ola Electric Q2 revenue falls 39% to Rs 421 crore
body: Ola Electric's Q2 FY27 revenue fell 39% to Rs 421 crore from Rs 690 crore a year earlier. Net loss narrowed 13% to Rs 362 crore. EV registrations fell 17% to 41,650 units. Scooter buyers and investors have been watching the company's sales slide.

title: Retail smartphone sales tanked 20% in Diwali week as prices jump, AIMRA says
body: The All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) says offline phone volumes fell 18-20% from Dhanteras (6 Nov) to the day after Diwali, while sales value stayed broadly flat because prices rose. Volumes in the seven days before Dhanteras fell nearly 40%. Most purchases were in the ₹30,000-60,000 band after offers. Per-device memory cost rose to $60-65 from about $20 in 2025, per a Jefferies report the page cites. Value-conscious buyers moved to HMD, Lava, Ai+, Tecno and itel, or to pre-owned and refurbished phones. Retailers said tighter loan underwriting meant only 60-70% of logged loan applications were approved, so many buyers could not complete purchases. AIMRA expects store volumes to fall by as much as 50% over the next three months.

title: Dhanteras 2026: gold sales hit ₹60,000 crore as buyers go lighter and smaller
body: Gold sales on Dhanteras are estimated at ₹60,000 crore, up 15-20% year on year, though quantity sold is expected to be roughly unchanged. Delhi 24-carat gold was ₹1.46 lakh per 10g on 6 Nov, against ₹1.32 lakh last Dhanteras and a ₹1.83 lakh peak on 29 Jan 2026. Silver sales were up 30% in value and 10% in volume, per a GJC estimate. Buyers favoured pendants, bangles, chains, 1-5 gram coins and 18-carat pieces, which were about half of one jeweller's sales. Younger buyers bought digital gold in small amounts, from as little as ₹10 on one platform. The article says higher prices still shape purchase decisions, and it has no direct quotes from individual buyers.

title: Diwali online retail sales grow 2% year on year while festive ad costs surge 62%, Criteo finds
body: Criteo says online retail sales in the two weeks before Diwali were up 2% on the same period last year, and about 30% above its 1-14 September 2026 baseline. Cost per click rose 62% and cost per thousand impressions 38% in that window. On Diwali day itself, CPC was up 83% and CPM up 65%. Unit-sales jumps for selected products included baby and toddler outerwear +205%, table runners +180%, candle holders +178% and food gift baskets +105%. The article warns that the 2% (year on year) and 30% (against a baseline) use different yardsticks, that the product jumps do not show category revenue, and that all figures come from Criteo alone.

title: Record October for autos: passenger vehicles cross 5 lakh, scooters up 31.6%
body: SIAM data shows domestic passenger vehicle sales of 5,19,060 units in October, up 12.4% and the first month above 5 lakh. Two-wheelers reached 25,77,810 units, up 16.1%, with scooters at 10,96,756 (+31.6%) and motorcycles at 14,23,118 (+6.6%). Three-wheelers rose 25.7% to 1,03,349. For April-October, domestic passenger vehicles are up 25.5% at 30,82,634 units. SIAM's Director General Rajesh Menon credited easier credit access and replacement purchases in both rural and urban markets for two-wheeler demand. These are wholesale dispatch figures, so they do not capture the retail picture.

title: Swiggy Q2: loss narrows to ₹922 crore as Instamart orders rise 29% and cheap-meal apps take off
body: Swiggy's July-September net loss narrowed 16% to ₹922 crore on revenue of ₹7,571 crore, up 36%. Instamart orders rose 29% to 130.3 million, with 14.8 million average monthly transacting users and 1,240 dark stores in 133 cities. Food delivery gross order value grew 18% to ₹10,054 crore. The company says its Bolt and ₹99 Store offers together made up over 25% of food-delivery volumes. Its affordable-meals app Toing, now in 50+ cities, is drawing mostly new or long-inactive users. Swiggy says Instamart's losses peaked this quarter after it spent on pricing to win back dormant users.

title: Eternal Q2: Blinkit order value jumps 79% to ₹20,940 crore as store count passes 2,700
body: Eternal reported Q2 net profit up 92.3% to ₹125 crore on revenue of ₹24,138 crore, up 77.6%. Blinkit's net order value rose 79.3% to ₹20,940 crore, and it ended the quarter with 2,751 stores after adding 308. Eternal now expects more than 3,500 Blinkit stores by March 2027 and about 5,000 by March 2028. Food delivery net order value rose 21.5% to ₹11,445 crore, with average monthly transacting customers at 28 million. Investors pushed the stock up about 2%, and the article says they will watch whether Blinkit can keep growing and stay profitable as it expands.

title: October GST collections jump 23% to ₹2.31 lakh crore, domestic sales up 15.8%
body: Gross GST collections in October were over ₹2,31,000 crore, up nearly 23% year on year. GST on domestic sales rose 15.8% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and import GST rose 42.2% to ₹72,246 crore. Refunds rose 6.5% to ₹27,934 crore, and net GST revenue rose 25.6% to ₹2.03 lakh crore. The report credits robust domestic economic activity and a sharp rise in import tax revenue. It describes the figures as provisional government data that may be revised.

title: Retail inflation hits two-year high of 6.09%; onions have doubled to ₹53.81 a kilo
body: MoSPI data released 12 November put October retail inflation at 6.09%, up from 5.5% in September and above the RBI's 6% upper limit. Food inflation was 8.94%, up from 7.74%. Rural inflation was 6.63% and urban 5.41%. Onions were ₹53.81 a kilo on 12 November against ₹26.91 a year earlier, and sugar was ₹60.40 against ₹46.59. The article blames erratic weather, El Niño-linked rainfall deficits, crop diseases and higher energy, fertiliser and transport costs tied to the West Asia conflict. It notes that rural households are hit harder than urban ones.

title: Calling rules in India: what changed on 18 October and what is due next
body: Under TRAI's amended telemarketing rules, which the page says went live around 18 October, enquiry leads get a seven-day window and transaction-support calls need explicit consent valid for seven days. Operators flag suspected spam numbers using AI/ML. From 1 November the Department of Telecommunications has directed operators to show caller names on 4G and above. Automated (A2P) calls must be declared to the operator in advance from about 17 November, and undeclared ones count as unsolicited commercial calls. The page says several dates are approximate and that it is not legal advice.

title: November 1 rule changes: ITR audit deadline, pension life certificates, GST and LPG explained
body: The income tax return deadline for audit cases moved from 31 October to 21 November 2026, but only for specified taxpayers whose accounts need an audit. Pensioners below 80 can submit life certificates from 1 November, with the window generally open until 30 November. GST changes from 1 November simplify rules for post-sale discounts and speed up provisional refunds for businesses. No official LPG price change had been announced as of 29 October. Cabinet-approved disability pension reforms would lower the minimum threshold from 80% to 40% and raise assistance to Rs 375 and Rs 625 per month, but they are not yet in force because operational guidelines are pending.

title: Delhi-NCR offices told to run at 50% in-person attendance until 20 November
body: The Commission for Air Quality Management ordered on 30 October that state and private offices in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Noida have at most 50% of staff in the office from 5 to 20 November. Industrial establishments and essential services are exempt. Delhi's AQI hit 377 on 4 November, and GRAP Stage II has applied since 2 November. Delhi's winter plan separately lists a 50% remote-work measure from 1 November, so several rules overlap. The reports leave open penalties, how firms should pick the 50%, and whether the window will be extended.

title: Delhi's winter curbs from 1 November: vehicle entry limits, doubled parking fees, 50% office attendance
body: From 1 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, Delhi restricts entry of vehicles below BS-VI and those without valid PUC certificates. The Transport Department estimates more than 10 lakh vehicles from Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida, Greater Noida and Ghaziabad could be affected. Enforcement uses ANPR cameras and e-challans, with possible impoundment. Parking fees at authorised lots double from 1 November to 28 February, with DMRC lots exempt. Outdoor construction is suspended, with a full construction and demolition ban from 10 December to 20 January. Physical office attendance is capped at 50%.

title: Karnataka to make digital meters mandatory for Ola, Uber, taxis and autos from the New Year
body: Karnataka's transport minister said app-based cabs such as Ola and Uber, private taxis and autorickshaws must use digital meters from the New Year, and vehicles without them will be seized. He said the aim is to curb one-sided fare-setting by aggregators, and airport trips without meters will be a specific target, with a 20-person enforcement squad. Footpath riding by two-wheelers will carry a fine of Rs 5,000 for a first offence and Rs 10,000 for a second, up from Rs 1,000. A statewide ban on half helmets is also planned. The rules are described as being in their final stages, and no commuter reactions are quoted.

title: NPCI revises UPI dispute rules: new reason codes, evidence requirements from 25 November
body: An NPCI circular dated 4 November (OC No. 240/2026-27) standardises how banks and apps handle UPI disputes, effective 25 November 2026. 'Wrong Credit Chargeback' is renamed 'Wrong Payment – Reversal Request'. New reason codes cover excess charges, duplicate or multiple transactions, cancelled or returned goods, and defective or undelivered goods or services. Supporting evidence such as payment receipts, purchase invoices, FIR/NCRP copies and customer confirmations is required depending on the dispute type. This is a legal-update summary aimed at banks, and it carries no user reactions.

title: US assures India lower tariffs than rivals in proposed trade deal
body: Citing a Bloomberg report, Business Today says the US has told India it will face lower tariffs than its trading peers under the proposed bilateral deal. Talks have run for nearly two years, and a framework for the first phase was finalised in February. The first phase covers goods only, with services to follow later. Formalising it has been delayed by several US trade investigations and by tensions over the Russian-oil tariff measure, which allows tariffs of up to 100% that are currently waived. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said an announcement could come 'quite soon'. He said India will not compromise on dairy market access or allow genetically modified products.

title: Petrol and diesel rates hold steady across metros on 19 November
body: Petrol and diesel prices were unchanged in the metros on 19 November. Delhi pays Rs 102.12 for petrol and Rs 95.20 for diesel per litre. Mumbai pays Rs 111.21 and Rs 97.83, and Chennai pays Rs 107.76 and Rs 99.55. Hyderabad is the dearest at Rs 115.69 for petrol and Rs 103.82 for diesel. The page only lists prices and carries no commentary on public reaction.

title: Commercial LPG and CNG get costlier as West Asia pressure lingers
body: The 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder rose by Rs 10 to Rs 17 from 1 November. It now costs Rs 2,820 in Delhi and Rs 2,971 in Kolkata. The 14.2-kg home cylinder is unchanged at Rs 942 in Delhi. Saudi Aramco raised its propane benchmark by $40 to $720 per tonne. CNG went up as well: Adani Total Gas raised it by as much as Rs 4.45/kg, and Mumbai's hike to Rs 90/kg is the sixth in seven months, which the article links to the West Asia conflict. Commercial LPG had already risen Rs 62.50 to Rs 71.50 the month before, so canteens, hostels and cab and auto drivers on CNG feel it.

title: Rupee strengthens to 93.51 on softer crude and foreign inflows
body: The rupee rose 43 paise to close at 93.51 per dollar (provisional) on 17 November, after closing at 93.94 the day before. The gain came from softer crude, with Brent at $92.79 a barrel, along with a positive domestic market and foreign fund inflows. A strong dollar and high US bond yields limited it. FIIs bought Rs 4,864.68 crore of equities on the previous trading day. An analyst expects USD/INR to trade between 93.20 and 93.75. A stronger rupee helps with imported fuel, foreign tuition and travel costs, but the page carries no public commentary.

title: Airlines cut seats in November despite the festive and wedding rush
body: IndiGo cut capacity from 13.1 million seats in October to 12.8 million in November, about 300,000 fewer. Industry capacity is down 2.5% on a year ago, with domestic down 3.3%. Air India's 3.3 million seats are 12.8% (483,000) fewer than last year, and SpiceJet cut 28.8%. Airlines blame high jet fuel prices and geopolitical uncertainty, which have also pushed fares up. IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh said forward bookings keep the third-quarter picture 'positive'.

title: Patna and Darbhanga hit hardest as airlines cut Diwali-season flights
body: Indian airlines scheduled 22,306 weekly domestic flights for November, down 606 (2.6%), according to Cirium data cited by Business Standard. Air India cut 543 weekly flights (14.9%) and IndiGo 375 (2.7%). Patna weekly departures fell from 377 to 302 and Hyderabad-Patna from 90 to 42, so migrants heading home to Bihar had fewer options. The article blames costlier aviation fuel, a weaker rupee and softer demand. Its baseline figures are internally inconsistent.

title: Samsung and Xiaomi raise phone prices by up to Rs 4,000 on memory-chip costs
body: Samsung and Xiaomi raised prices on 48 phone variants by Rs 1,000 to Rs 4,000, effective 15-16 November. The Galaxy A57 got the steepest Samsung hike, with its 8GB+256GB variant now at Rs 66,999. The article ties the rises to memory-chip costs driven by global AI data-centre demand. Smartphone sales volumes fell as much as 20% year on year during the 6-9 November festive period, according to AIMRA. Offline volumes fell nearly 40% in the week before Dhanteras. Higher prices are squeezing budget and mid-range buyers.

title: Ramayana Part 1 sets a record Diwali week at the box office
body: Sacnilk estimates Ramayana earned Rs 930 crore worldwide in seven days, with Rs 605 crore gross in India. It calls this the biggest Diwali week at the Indian box office. The Tamil film Scene added Rs 190 crore worldwide in six days, taking the two films to Rs 1,120+ crore combined. The film's strength came from Hindi business plus South Indian dubbed versions. The figures are estimates. Siasat's coverage says reception on social media was mixed, with Yash's Ravana praised and some questioning the casting of Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi.

title: GTA 6 lands in India: Rs 5,999 game, but about Rs 70,989 with a PS5
body: Store listings put GTA 6 at Rs 5,999 for the Standard Edition and Rs 7,499 for Ultimate, with a midnight IST launch on 19 November that Rockstar has not confirmed. The catch is the console: a PS5 Slim Digital is Rs 64,990, so day one costs about Rs 70,989. The console makes up about 92% of the spend. The disc PS5 costs Rs 4,995 more for a drive the game won't use at launch. There is no PC version announced, and the free GTA+ month needs a digital pre-order before 20 November.

title: Chhath rush: full trains, Patna flights above Rs 44,000 and 77 buses falling short
body: Migrant workers raced home for Chhath, which runs 13 to 16 November. East Central Railway is running 103 pairs of special trains. One day saw 37,698 tickets bought for Surat's Udhna-Jaynagar trains. Delhi-Patna flights start around Rs 15,367 and Mumbai-Patna around Rs 18,401, with some Patna fares above Rs 44,000. Holding areas were set up at Anand Vihar and New Delhi stations, and the headline says the 77 buses from Anand Vihar are also not enough.

title: Fans fume as Rohit, Kohli and Iyer all fall for ducks in 4th ODI
body: Chasing 334 at Bay Oval, India were 0/3 after the first over, as Matt Henry took a triple-wicket maiden. Rohit Sharma was out on the first ball, Virat Kohli bowled for a four-ball duck and Shreyas Iyer fell on the last ball. India were later 9/4 in the 6th over. Fans posted anger and sarcasm online, and some said Rohit and Kohli should have retired three years ago. Many others still want the 'Ro-Ko' pair at the 2027 ODI World Cup. Iyer was also criticised for choosing to bowl first.

title: Suriya's Scene crosses Rs 145 crore in three days, a Diwali Tamil hit
body: The makers claim Scene, released on 6 November, grossed Rs 145 crore worldwide in three days. It is Suriya's third straight 2026 success after Karuppu and Vishwanath & Sons. The action comedy, directed by Jithu Madhavan, also marks Nazriya Nazim's return to Tamil films after 12 years. Independent tracker Sacnilk gave a lower estimate, though the article gives no figure. Suriya and Jyotika thanked fans in a joint Instagram post, with Suriya crediting audiences across languages and borders.

title: ISL's opening week drew 65 million YouTube views in five matches. Is India ready for football?
body: The 2026-27 Indian Super League drew 65 million YouTube views and 52 million reach across its first five fixtures. The page says views can include repeat watching. NorthEast United vs Mohun Bagan Super Giant alone got 19.27 million views, and about 91% of the opening audience watched on phones. Stadium crowds were thinner than the online numbers: 40,014 watched Kerala Blasters draw with Mumbai City in Kochi, and 3,459 attended Inter Kashi vs Kerala Blasters in Pune. NorthEast United owner John Abraham says India is ready for football and predicts 'the stands are going to fill up completely'. The page notes that the attendance figures will show whether free streaming turns into ticket sales. The page itself carries no fan comments.

title: Sports bulletin Nov 11: Hamilton ODI washed out, Pant close to Test return, Sanju to captain Kerala
body: The third ODI against New Zealand in Hamilton was abandoned without a ball bowled, which left India 2-0 up in the five-match series. The washout also ended New Zealand's 11-series home ODI winning run, which began in 2019. Rishabh Pant is reportedly close to returning to the Test squad pending fitness tests. Sanju Samson will captain Kerala in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, which starts on November 24. Aaryavir Sehwag scored 160 off 168 balls against the UAE in the U19 Asia Cup, with 17 fours and seven sixes, and India made 309/7. The page reports on the news and does not quote fans. Cricket followers will be watching Pant's fitness and the domestic T20 season.

title: India defend 209 to beat New Zealand by 22 runs and win ODI series 3-1
body: India were bowled out for 209 in the fifth ODI at Mount Maunganui and then bowled New Zealand out for 187 in 48.1 overs to win by 22 runs and take the series 3-1. Arshdeep Singh took 3-30 and was Player of the Match, Siraj and Axar Patel took two wickets each, and debutant Yash Thakur took his first ODI wicket. Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan each scored 46. The result ended New Zealand's run of 11 consecutive home bilateral ODI series wins, which began after India's 4-1 win in 2019. It came two days after India's collapse in the fourth ODI, so the comeback was seen as a relief. The page has no fan quotes.

title: BCCI reportedly weighing two new IPL teams for 2028, with Pune and Vadodara as options
body: The BCCI is reportedly considering two new franchises before the 2028 mega auction, which would take the IPL from 10 teams to 12. Pune and Vadodara are named as possible homes. Industry estimates put each new franchise at about ₹8,800 crore. Talks are described as 'at an early stage' and no formal decision has been made. Reports also mention a possible January start and a longer, two-phase season, with the media rights deal due before the 2028 auction. Separately, another outlet reported on November 12 that the BCCI denied discussing a 12-team IPL, so fans are hearing mixed signals. The page has no fan reaction.

title: Carlsen slips, Caruana closes in at Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot in Budapest
body: Magnus Carlsen lost 15.8 rating points and fell to 2,807.2 in the live ratings after five draws and a loss in the Fast Classical section. He has been world No. 1 since July 2011. Fabiano Caruana gained 17 points to reach 2,800, which is 7.2 behind Carlsen. Indian players had a mixed week: Arjun Erigaisi won and drew against Wesley So and is third in Group D. R Vaishali recorded her first win but is bottom of Group D. R Praggnanandhaa has 4 points from four draws and two losses. The top four in each group advance to the title stage. The page carries no fan comments.

title: 2026 becomes India's highest-grossing box-office year ever, with six weeks still left
body: Sacnilk's estimates through November 15 put India's 2026 box office at ₹13,775 Cr, about ₹425 Cr ahead of 2025's ₹13,350 Cr. Top grossers are Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge at ₹1,375 Cr, Ramayana at ₹909 Cr, Spider-Man: Brand New Day at ₹599.25 Cr, Jailer 2 at ₹555.25 Cr and Drishyam 3 at ₹455.75 Cr. Hindi is 44% of the total, Telugu 18% and Tamil 15%. The article credits mid-budget South films, three Suriya hits and record Malayalam numbers. It warns that business is concentrated in a few big films while many smaller releases struggle. The year needs about ₹1,225 Cr more to reach ₹15,000 Cr.

title: Ramayana Part One opens at ₹127.50 crore worldwide, short of Adipurush and Dhurandhar 2
body: Ramayana: Part One opened on November 5 with Day 1 net of ₹64.85 crore across 25,200 shows, per Sacnilk, and ₹127.50 crore worldwide. Hindi contributed ₹47.50 crore. The article compares this with Dhurandhar 2 at ₹102 crore, Adipurush at ₹86.75 crore and Jawan at ₹75 crore. It reports 'houseful shows' on Thursday morning in many parts of India and calls the opening 'bumper'. The comparison with earlier films is the main debate, since the headline says it fell short of them. The page gives no audience reviews.

title: Top 5 Indian box office weekend (Nov 6-8): Ramayana leads with 69% share
body: Ramayana made ₹174.00 Cr net over the weekend of Nov 6-8, bringing its total to ₹238.85 Cr. Suriya's Scene was second with ₹63.15 Cr, and Mookuthi Amman 2 made ₹8.95 Cr. The top five together made ₹252.75 Cr net. The piece says Ramayana's Kannada and Telugu dubs helped and that its Saturday jumped after a weaker Friday. It says its Hindi version softened. Scene grew over the weekend through word of mouth and strong support in Kerala, and Mookuthi Amman 2 rose sharply on Sunday. The article warns that business is concentrated in the top two films and says weekday holds are the next test.

title: First Monday box office: Ramayana leads nationally, Suriya's Scene dominates South India
body: Ramayana made ₹107.50 crore net on its fifth day, a Monday jump of 91.5% after Diwali. Scene made ₹21.25 crore on Day 4, a 10.1% drop from its Sunday ₹23.65 crore. In Tamil Nadu, Scene made ₹17.85 crore against ₹4 crore for Ramayana's Tamil version. Ramayana's five-day worldwide figure is ₹663.90 crore, and Scene's four-day worldwide gross is ₹150 crore. The writer reads Scene's Tamil Nadu lead as 'strong support' for the Suriya film. The page has no audience quotes.

title: Jailer 2 on Prime Video: viewers split on whether it is overrated
body: Jailer 2 began streaming on Prime Video on November 12, and viewers were split. Some called it overrated, said the screenplay was predictable and said Rajinikanth's presence was the only thing carrying a mediocre commercial entertainer. Others found the cameos weak and boring. Defenders said theatre-crowd comedy doesn't land at home and still called it a good commercial entertainer. A separate Filmibeat piece dated November 14 says fans praised the Hrithik Roshan cameo and the interval sequence.

title: Jailer 2 on Prime Video: fans celebrate Rajinikanth, call Hrithik Roshan's cameo a highlight
body: After Jailer 2 reached Prime Video, fans on social media praised Rajinikanth's screen presence and its mass appeal. One viewer gave the coffee-revenge scene four stars and called the film a blockbuster. Another said Nelson handled the veteran star well given his age and singled out the interval sequence. Hrithik Roshan's cameo as Roddy drew the strongest praise, with one fan calling it the film's best part for its swagger and aura. Several viewers were simply glad to rewatch it at home. The Sacnilk theatrical chart dated Nov 9 puts Jailer 2's India total at ₹470.40 Cr.

title: Satinder Sartaaj's 'Guzarish' hits No. 1 on YouTube's global songs chart
body: For the week ending November 12, 'Guzarish' by Satinder Sartaaj topped YouTube's global songs chart with 42,613,776 views, up from 28,263,770 the week before. India supplied 32,326,244 of those views, or 75.9%. It premiered on September 16 on T-Series and climbed slowly over eight weeks. The article ties the late surge to Diwali on November 8 and the first full week of Ramayana in cinemas. Diljit Dosanjh's 'POKITO' with Daddy Yankee fell from No. 3 to No. 64. The article notes that the official video makes up only about half of the song's chart total.

title: New OTT releases Nov 9-15: Jailer 2, Daayra, Ranabaali and more
body: This week's streaming slate included Jailer 2 on Prime Video (Nov 12), Meghna Gulzar's Daayra with Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran on Netflix (Nov 13), and Vijay Deverakonda's Ranabaali on Netflix (Nov 13). JioHotstar added Student of the Year: After Dark with Shanaya Kapoor, and Prime Video put out Rings of Power Season 3. Daayra and Ranabaali were released in theatres weeks earlier. The page is a release list and carries no audience reactions. It shows what people had on their screens during the Diwali week.

title: Salesforce layoffs in India: Employees get garden leave, share exit terms and check severance
body: Salesforce employees in India hit by a new round of job cuts are sharing exit terms on the anonymous platform Blind. One account describes about two months of garden leave (paid time away from work), and others mention severance of "around 21 weeks". One affected employee said they would be on garden leave until February 1 and wrote, "Got laid off and currently going through tough time processing it." The number of people affected is unknown, and the figures come from employee posts, not from Salesforce. Laid-off staff are asking for job referrals in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Mumbai.

title: Qualcomm CEO Calls India Layoffs 'Performance-Focused', But Employees Allege Favouritism
body: Qualcomm's India layoffs reportedly began on November 9. CEO Cristiano Amon called them a "performance-focused reduction" in an internal memo. A Blind analysis of anonymous posts found 47.7% of layoff-related discussions cited politics or favouritism, against 34.2% that cited cost or performance. Employees allege middle managers favoured people from their own hometowns or language groups, and that remote workers and people on medical or maternity leave were targeted. Staff were also unhappy about the timing so close to Diwali. The article says the 47.7% is a share of online discussion, not of affected employees. It adds that the posts are unverified and Qualcomm has not responded to the allegations. Reports say more than 1,000 roles could be at risk, but Qualcomm has not confirmed that.

title: Tide to pivot India operations following strategic review
body: Tide announced it will wind down its member-facing business in India after a strategic review. About 400 colleagues are affected. The page says the company has had more than one million India members since December 2022. Its Hyderabad centre of excellence, with about 800 employees, stays open. The page cites a target of about £250 million India investment by the end of 2030. This is the company's own announcement, so I found no worker reaction on the page.

title: Freshers are not disappearing, their jobs are changing: Cognizant India chief on AI's impact on hiring
body: Cognizant India chairman Rajesh Varrier says AI is changing entry-level work, from doing tasks to validating AI output, rather than removing it. A June 2026 Cognizant and Pearson study found 37% of entry-level tasks in India's large organisations are already done by AI, against a 33% global average. Cognizant plans to hire about 24,000-25,000 freshers in 2026, versus about 20,000 in 2025. Headcount was 359,900 as of September 30, 2026, up 10,100 from a year earlier. This is the company's own framing of a fear many young job-seekers have. The article quotes no freshers.

title: White-collar hiring rises 14% in October, manufacturing and production roles lead: Naukri JobSpeak
body: White-collar hiring rose 14% year-on-year in October 2026, with the Naukri JobSpeak Index at 2,836 against 2,480 a year earlier. Part of the gain reflects a weak base, because Diwali fell in October 2025. IT and software services hiring grew only 5%, while AI and machine learning roles rose 32%. Production hiring across industries rose 39%, and freshers rose 15%. Candidates with 13–16 years of experience saw 22% growth. The picture for office workers is uneven: the headline is strong but it is led by factory and production roles, not software jobs.

title: ADP People at Work 2026: India Tops AI Use At 41%, Unpaid Work At 24%
body: ADP's report is based on a 2025 survey of more than 39,000 workers in 36 markets. It finds 80% of Indian workers use AI multiple times a week and 41% use it almost daily. 24% of Indian workers do 16 or more unpaid hours a week, against 12% globally. 30% of Indian workers strongly agree their job is safe, against 22% globally. Within India that confidence is 37% for knowledge workers but only 17-18% for skilled-task and repetitive-task workers. The article says daily AI users are 4x more likely than non-users to feel less productive, even though they are more engaged. The article contradicts itself on India's job-security rank, third in the text but second in its table.

title: Instagram Lets Users Edit Stories 15 Minutes After Posting And Add Affiliate Links To Reels
body: Instagram is rolling out story edits in stages: users can change text, music, stickers and drawings for 15 minutes after posting, and edited Stories carry an "Edited" label. Creators can also add trackable affiliate product links to Reels, posts, Stories, DMs and bios, and Instagram says it takes no cut. In India the partners are Flipkart and Myntra. Creators must be 18 or older, have a public professional account, live in India, and have more than 2,000 followers. The page reports the feature changes but no creator reactions.

title: Instagram changes what Indians see: What Meta's new content rules mean for users
body: Instagram has tightened default protections in India so recommendations from accounts users don't follow show less sexually suggestive and violent content across Explore, Reels and Feed. Meta says people in India now flag recommended content about half as often as a year ago. It has not released the underlying figures or method. The change follows a October 10 MeitY advisory on ranking and recommendation systems, though Meta has not tied the two together. Teen Accounts in India default to a 13-plus content setting. The article notes outside observers cannot measure the scale of the change from what Meta shared.

title: Meta brings long-form videos to Instagram: Should YouTube be worried?
body: Instagram is testing "Features", a format letting selected creators upload horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes, which could suit podcasts, interviews and comedy shows. The test began with selected creators in Brazil and is expanding to a small group in the US. The article notes Indian creators should not assume they have access. YouTube's Partner Programme gives eligible creators 55% of net ad revenue, while a Meta spokesperson said it is "too early to share a long-term monetization model". The article advises Indian creators to test the format but keep YouTube as their main home for full-length videos.

title: ₹3.06 lakh from 5 brand deals: Kolkata content creator reveals her earnings
body: Kolkata creator Sayantika Bhowmick said in an Instagram video that she earned ₹3.06 lakh from five brand collaborations in October 2026, with Tira, Myntra Beauty, Sprite, Pilgrim and LoveChild by Masaba. She kept her workload light during Durga Puja and undercharged on some deals because of the brand's name. She had not yet been paid, because brand payments typically take 30 to 45 days. She said, "I haven't got the money yet because of the payment timeline, which is 30 to 45 days." The article shows no wider audience reaction.

title: India's creator economy in numbers: what brands should know this November
body: The piece says India has roughly 4 million active creators, about two-thirds of them outside the metros. Paid influencer marketing is estimated at about ₹3,400–3,500 crore in 2026. It cites industry data that creators contributed over ₹18,000 crore of GDP in 2025 and about one million jobs. It also cites a survey finding two-thirds of creators globally earn under $10,000 a year from content. It states India has not passed a "National Creator Economy Bill" and that posts claiming otherwise are false. This is a brand-side blog, so there is no creator reaction on the page.

title: Shanaya Kapoor Laughs Off Viral 'Everybody's From The Village' Trend
body: A sarcastic video by creator Divyanshi Chauhan mocking people who look down on villagers turned "Everybody's from the village, Shanaya" into an online punchline against class snobbery. Actor Shanaya Kapoor responded by posting a video of herself laughing at the roasts. She joked, "I just spent six episodes trying to solve a murder, what did I do to your ancestors." She also used the moment to promote her six-episode series Student Of The Year: After Dark, which premiered on JioHotstar on November 13, 2026. She made a transition reel with Orry as well.

title: Udaipur man who asked Thai-French YouTuber JustKeth for 'lip kiss' during livestream issues apology, says he is 'deeply ashamed'
body: A clip of a man repeatedly asking Thai-French streamer JustKeth for a kiss during a night livestream in Udaipur went viral. A separate Aaj Tak report dated November 16 says it was viewed over 50 lakh (5 million) times. She refused and had posted it with the caption "At least he asked". The man, identifying himself as Aftab, apologised in a video and said, "I am deeply ashamed of the mistake I have made." He says he was arrested. Online users criticised his behaviour. Many said a clear no should be respected, and the case reopened talk about how women and foreign tourists are treated in public.

title: 'Please Take Public Transport Next Time': Sonam Kapoor Gets Trolled Over 'Buy Less Cars' Remark At Earthshot Prize Awards 2026
body: At the Earthshot Prize Awards 2026 in Mumbai, Sonam Kapoor told reporters people should cut car use, avoid plastic and keep rivers clean. Instagram users mocked her advice and pointed to her jewellery and clothes. One commented, "Sonam please take public transport next time (sic)." Another wrote, "She's asking us to buy less cars - she didn't say she herself is going to buy less cars (sic)." The article has no statistics. It shows how quickly online audiences call out celebrity sermons seen as hypocritical.
